title.analysis: Exact original: The Money Skills School Never Taught You And Why It’s Costing You. Institutional omission plus personal loss creates curiosity about missing skills and financial consequences. No numerical threshold, concrete skill or promised timeframe; broad educational grievance and beginner intent. Script delivers a catalogue and critique, with fewer operational worked lessons than the title could imply.

thumbnail.analysis: Inspected 1280x720 and 320px. White background, huge black SCHOOL NEVER / TAUGHT THIS across top/right; thoughtful cartoon man left, green note and coins dropping toward savings jar lower middle, five worried cartoon people amid pink money lower right, two wearing graduation caps, large black curved arrow points toward group. Clear headline and figure hierarchy; small money/group detail loses clarity at mobile width. Green accumulation versus pink overwhelmed graduates suggests education protects wealth, repeats school omission rather than naming a skill. No numeric loss or actual photographed face. Matches script graduation motif and grievance, not proof of educational causation. Current saved image cannot certify upload-era design.

script.analysis: All 22209 stored characters read in seven contiguous bounded ranges and source hash matched. Opens imagined graduation-to-paycheck shock, FAKA credit-score confusion and school-subject contrasts; self-introduction and early subscribe CTA precede curriculum critique. No timed segments: first 30 seconds cannot be certified. Progresses budget/credit/compounding → taxes/credits → student loans → assets/housing → political manipulation/income taxation → psychology/negotiation → gig work/insurance → self-education and subscribe/share. Repeated school-versus-life contrasts, rhetorical questions, racecar/quicksand/nutrition metaphors and outrage sustain thematic continuity, but mostly serial modules rather than one resolved narrative. Concrete dollar stakes heighten emotion; compounding payoff contains order-of-magnitude error. No mid-course community advertisement observed in this text. Ending available through education system has not figured that out, with no final punctuation; all available text read, original audio completeness unknown.

claim_audit: At characters 7000–10500, $500 monthly for 40 years at nominal 7% compounded monthly gives $1,312,406.70, not over $13 million; deposits $240000. At effective annual 7% the result is lower still. Possible ASR decimal omission remains unresolvable without audio; stored text not corrected.

At 3500–7000, $100 monthly at nominal 6% from 15 to assumed retirement 65 gives $378719.11 versus $199149.07 starting 25. Nearly400k/200k broadly rounded; retirement age is unstated. Extra10years adds $12000 contributions, so total dollars contributed also differ. Returns hypothetical, no guarantee/inflation/taxes modeled.

Credit $1000/18%/minimum repayment >5years/$800 interest cannot be reproduced without minimum-payment formula, fee assumptions and no new charges. A fixed25 monthly payment clears in about62months with about539 interest; this illustrates sensitivity, not competitor actual contract. 50/30/20 percentages sum100, but take-home/gross basis not specified and applicability conditional.

NGPF primary 2024 release reports26.3% guaranteed standalone course access, a specific public-school population and implementation measure; 30 enacted states does not itself imply75% uneducated, and course access, mandate and compound-interest knowledge are different outcomes. Search result for late2025 supports30 states but current pages not upload snapshots. Alabama2013 decision improvement and68/31 teen percentages unverified here; not causal proof. Universal schools teach none contradicts acknowledged mandates.

IRS education-credit table supports maxima2500 per eligible student AOTC /2000 per return LLC, subject to qualified expenses, eligibility, income and dependent rules. LLC nonrefundable, AOTC partially refundable; not everyone gets freecash or both for same student/expenses. Retrieved current page is not contemporaneous capture.

37k average graduate debt lacks defined borrower denominator/year. 37k→50k total10year payments depends APR and schedule; deferment interest/capitalization conditional, not universal compound accrual. College opportunity-cost example omits earnings/career differences and counterfactual contributions.

Cashflow asset/liability rhetoric is not balance-sheet classification: an owner-occupied house/car can be an asset while loan is liability.300k→600k housing cost and1500rent comparison omit mortgage rate/downpayment, rent inflation, terminal home value, taxes and invested difference; no demonstrated renter advantage.

Investment-income lower-tax generalization overbroad: ordinary interest/nonqualified dividends/short-term gains differ from qualified dividends/long-term gains; business income not automatically preferential. Small salary/dividend strategy requires entity and compensation rules not explained. Earned income not invariably highest effective tax. IRS investment-income guidance distinguishes dividend categories.

One negotiation yields average1million lifetime gain unsourced; salary base, raise, compounding and years absent. Everything negotiable is rhetorical, not contractual guarantee. Political/school motives, national hundreds-of-billions cost, educator confidence and behavioral primacy unverified assertions. Genuine income constraints and institutional access are alternative explanations for outcomes. ASR FAKA, PO, 5030 and a regular income may be transcription artifacts, not certified spoken errors.
